Architectural Design & Prototype
The frontend uses the Presentation Tier of the layered architecture, built with ASP.NET Core MVC and Razor Views to create a dynamic, server-rendered application. This approach was selected for its seamless integration with the C# backend, security features (like built-in CSRF protection), and compatibility with Visual Studio.

The design is based on the provided prototype repository: https://github.com/SiyandaNduze/UniCribz-Web-app.git.

Design System:

Framework: ASP.NET Core MVC with Razor Views (.cshtml).

CSS Framework: Bootstrap 5 for a responsive, mobile-first grid system.

Color Scheme:

Primary: #2C3E50 (Dark Blue) - For headers, primary buttons, and navigation.

Secondary: #18BC9C (Teal Green) - For call-to-action buttons, accents, and highlights.

Background: #F8F9FA (Off-White) - For main content areas.

Text: #333333 (Dark Grey) - For standard body text.

Layout: A consistent layout via _Layout.cshtml featuring a top navigation bar, a main content container, and a footer. The layout adapts to show role-appropriate navigation links (e.g., a Tenant sees "My Dashboard," an Admin sees "Admin Portal").

Other Members' Responsibilities
Siyanda Nduze: Backend core, API development, deployment, DevOps, and initial repo setup.

Step-by-Step Implementation Guide
Step 1: Setup and Configure the ASP.NET Core MVC Project

In Visual Studio, open the UniCribz.sln solution created by Siyanda.

Add a new project: UniCribz.Web (ASP.NET Core Web App (Model-View-Controller)).

Set the project as the startup project.

Add the UniCribz.Api project as a project reference to UniCribz.Web.

Step 2: Create the Layout and Navigation

Open Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml.

Add the Bootstrap CSS/JS and your custom site.css.

Create a responsive navigation bar. Use Razor logic (@if (User.Identity.IsAuthenticated)) to conditionally show navigation links based on the user's role (Visitor, Tenant, Admin).

Step 3: Build the Public Facing Pages

Create the PropertyController.

Create a PropertySearchViewModel to hold search criteria (location, price range, property type).

Create the Views/Property/Search.cshtml view. Use HTML forms to capture search input and display a list of property cards. Each card will show the image, price, location, and key amenities.

Create the Views/Property/Details.cshtml view to show a single property's full details, including a photo gallery, map, and an "Apply" button.

Step 4: Implement the Application Form

Create the ApplicationController and an ApplicationViewModel.

Build the Views/Application/Create.cshtml view as a multi-step form using Bootstrap tabs or a wizard-style UI. The form will capture user details, preferences, and allow for document uploads.

On form submission, the controller will make an HTTP POST request to the backend API (UniCribz.Api) to create the application.

Step 5: Build the Tenant Dashboard

Create a TenantController.

Create a TenantDashboardViewModel to aggregate data (outstanding balance, lease details, open maintenance requests).

Build the Views/Tenant/Dashboard.cshtml view. Use dashboard cards and tables to display this information clearly. Include action buttons like "Upload Proof of Payment" and "Log Maintenance Request."

Architectural Design
You are responsible for the Application Tier's integration with external services. This includes:

Payment Gateway Integration: Implementing a service to handle rental payments. This involves redirecting users to a secure payment page, handling callbacks, and updating the Payment record status.

Notification System: Implementing the Strategy Pattern for notifications. You will create a NotificationManager and concrete strategies (EmailNotificationStrategy, SMSNotificationStrategy, InAppNotificationStrategy). This allows the system to send notifications through multiple channels without changing the core business logic.

Google Maps Integration: Implementing a service that calls the Google Maps API to provide location data for property search and details pages.

Other Members' Responsibilities
Siyanda Nduze: Backend core, API development, deployment, DevOps.

Siyabonga Cebekhulu: Database schema design and implementation.

Step-by-Step Implementation Guide
Step 1: Research and Documentation

Conduct the accommodation research as outlined in Task 1.1.1. Analyze competitors and validate business hypotheses. Document findings.

Step 2: Implement the Notification Strategy

In the UniCribz.Api project, create the INotificationStrategy interface with a send(recipient, message) method.

Create EmailNotificationStrategy, SMSNotificationStrategy, and InAppNotificationStrategy classes that implement this interface.

Create a NotificationManager class that takes a list of INotificationStrategy in its constructor. It will have a notifyTenant method that iterates through the strategies and calls send on each.

Step 3: Implement the Payment Service

Create an IPaymentService interface and a PaymentService class.

Integrate with a payment gateway provider (e.g., Stripe, PayFast). Use their .NET SDK.

Create a PaymentController with an endpoint to initiate a payment. This endpoint will create a Payment record with a Pending status and return a redirect URL to the gateway.

Create a callback endpoint to handle the gateway's response, update the Payment status to Verified or Failed, and trigger a notification.

Step 4: Implement Google Maps Integration

Create an IGoogleMapsService and GoogleMapsService.

Use the Google Maps .NET API client to geocode property addresses into latitude and longitude coordinates, which are stored in the database.

Create an API endpoint that returns property coordinates. Samkelsiwe will consume this endpoint to render markers on the map.

Step 5: Configure API Keys

Store all external API keys (Google Maps, Payment Gateway) in appsettings.json for local development.

Use Azure Key Vault or GitHub Secrets for secure storage in the staging and production environments.

Architectural Design
You are responsible for the Data Tier (Persistence Layer) of the system.

Primary Database: Azure Database for PostgreSQL (Flexible Server). Chosen for its ACID compliance, support for complex queries, and robust relational data modeling.

Data Access: Entity Framework Core with the Npgsql provider. This ORM provides a productive, C#-centric way to interact with the database while maintaining clean separation of concerns through the Repository Pattern.

Schema Design: The schema will be based on the Domain Class Diagram and ERD from the project document. All entities will have UUID primary keys, generated by the application. Relationships and constraints will be enforced through Fluent API configurations in OnModelCreating.

Other Members' Responsibilities
Siyanda Nduze: Backend core, API development, deployment, DevOps.

Anothile Bhengu: External API integrations and service logic.

Samkelsiwe Hlatshwayo: Frontend UI/UX design and implementation.

Step-by-Step Implementation Guide
Step 1: Set Up the Data Project and EF Core

Create a new Class Library project named UniCribz.Data in the solution.

Install the required NuGet packages: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design, Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL.

Add a reference to UniCribz.Data from the UniCribz.Api project.

Step 2: Define Entities and DbContext

In the Entities folder, create a C# class for each entity from the Domain Class Diagram (User, Property, Room, Lease, etc.). Use properties that map to the required data fields.

Create UniCribzDbContext.cs that inherits from DbContext.

Add a DbSet<T> property for each entity.

Override OnModelCreating to configure relationships and constraints using the Fluent API. For example, modelBuilder.Entity<Room>().HasOne(r => r.Property).WithMany(p => p.Rooms).

Step 3: Create and Apply Migrations

In the Package Manager Console (PMC) in Visual Studio, run Add-Migration InitialCreate.

This will generate a migration file in the Migrations folder. Review it to ensure it correctly reflects your schema.

Run Update-Database to apply the migration to your local development database.

Step 4: Implement the Repository Pattern

Create an IRepository<T> interface with methods like GetById, GetAll, Add, Update, Delete.

Create a Repository<T> class that implements this interface, using the UniCribzDbContext for data operations.

Register the repository in the Program.cs of the UniCribz.Api project for dependency injection.

Step 5: Data Migration Planning

Create a docs folder and add a data-migration-plan.md.

Outline the process for extracting data from the current spreadsheets/systems, cleaning it, and mapping it to the new schema.

Write a SQL script or a C# data migration tool (using EF Core) to load the cleaned data into a staging database for validation before the real cutover.

Architectural Design
You are responsible for the Application Tier and the overall system architecture.

Architecture Pattern: Layered (N-Tier) Architecture. The system is organized into Presentation (Frontend), Application (Backend API), and Data (Database) tiers. This provides clear separation of concerns.

API Design: The Application Tier will expose a RESTful API. This API will be the single point of contact for the frontend, enforcing all business rules and access controls.

Security: You will implement the security architecture, including:

Authentication: JWT (JSON Web Tokens) for stateless authentication.

Authorization: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with policies for Visitor, Tenant, and Admin.

OWASP Protections: Implementation of input validation, parameterized queries (via EF Core), and output encoding to prevent XSS, SQL Injection, and other common threats.

Deployment: You will lead the DevOps effort, implementing a CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions for automated builds, tests, and deployments to Azure. The deployment strategy is Blue-Green, ensuring zero-downtime releases and easy rollbacks.

Step-by-Step Implementation Guide
Step 1: Initial Repository and Solution Setup (Your Primary Task)

Create a new repository on GitHub named UniCribz-Student-Accommodation-System.

Clone the repository to your local machine.

Create a new Visual Studio solution named UniCribz.

Create a staging branch from the main branch. This branch will be the integration branch for all features before they are merged into main for a production release. Set up branch protection rules for main and staging to require pull request reviews and passing CI checks.

Initialize the project structure:

UniCribz.Api (ASP.NET Core Web API)

UniCribz.Data (Class Library for EF Core)

UniCribz.Web (ASP.NET Core MVC for Frontend)

UniCribz.Shared (Class Library for shared DTOs and Models)

Add all projects to the solution and set up the project references (e.g., UniCribz.Api references UniCribz.Data and UniCribz.Shared).

Step 2: Configure Dependencies

In UniCribz.Api, install necessary NuGet packages: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Tools, Swashbuckle.AspNetCore (for Swagger).

In UniCribz.Data, install Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL.

Configure Program.cs to set up services: Add DbContext, configure JWT authentication, add controllers with views, and set up CORS policy for the frontend.

Step 3: Implement Core API and Security

Create your first controller, AuthController, with endpoints for Register and Login. Use ASP.NET Core Identity or a custom user management service.

Implement JWT token generation on successful login. Configure the [Authorize] attribute with roles on your controllers to enforce RBAC.

Create a PropertyController with CRUD endpoints. Use the repository from the Data project to interact with the database.

Step 4: Set Up the CI/CD Pipeline

In the .github/workflows/ directory, create ci.yml. This workflow will run on every push to a feature/* branch and on pull requests to staging. It will:

Check out the code.

Set up the .NET SDK.

Run dotnet restore, dotnet build, and dotnet test.

Create deploy-staging.yml. This workflow will run when code is pushed to the staging branch. It will:

Build and publish the application.

Deploy the artifacts to the Azure Staging environment.

Run automated smoke tests.

Create deploy-production.yml. This workflow will be triggered by a new tag on the main branch (e.g., v1.0.0). It will implement the Blue-Green deployment strategy:

Deploy the new version to the "Green" environment.

Run health checks.

Switch traffic from "Blue" to "Green" using Azure Traffic Manager or Application Gateway.

Include a manual approval step for the traffic switch.

Step 5: Configure Azure Infrastructure

Use Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with ARM templates or Terraform. Store these files in an azure-pipelines or infrastructure folder.

Define resources: Azure App Service (or VMSS), Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure Cache for Redis, Azure Blob Storage, Azure Application Gateway, and Azure VNet with subnets.

Configure Network Security Groups (NSGs) to restrict traffic between subnets (e.g., the database subnet should only accept traffic from the application subnet).

Step 6: Deployment Verification

After the pipeline runs, verify the deployment by checking the health endpoint of the API.

Monitor the Azure Application Insights dashboard for any errors or performance degradation.

Test a few key user journeys (e.g., login, search for a property) to ensure the new version is functioning correctly.

Project Overview
UniCribz is a cloud-native Student Accommodation Management System designed to solve South Africa's student housing crisis. It provides a unified digital platform connecting students seeking accommodation with lodging operators, replacing fragmented manual processes (spreadsheets, paper applications, WhatsApp groups) with a single source of truth.

Core Features
Visitor Portal: Browse, filter, and search accommodation with Google Maps integration

Smart Room Allocation: Automated vacancy tracking and room assignment engine

Application Workflow: Digital applications with document uploads and status tracking

Tenant Dashboard: Lease management, payment history, maintenance requests

Admin Portal: Centralized management of properties, tenants, applications, payments, and reports

Notification System: Multi-channel (Email, SMS, In-App) notifications via Strategy Pattern

Payment Processing: Upload proof of payment, verification, and receipting

Maintenance & Complaints: Full lifecycle tracking with status workflows

Problem Statement
South Africa faces a critical student accommodation shortage:

Only ~20% of university students have access to on-campus housing (vs. 50% global norm)

Shortage of 500,000+ student beds nationally

At University of Johannesburg alone: ~100,000 applicants for 7,015 beds

Students resort to homeless conditions, subpar housing, or expensive long-distance commuting

Private accommodation management uses disjointed manual processes (spreadsheets, email, paper, WhatsApp)

Solution Summary
UniCribz eliminates fragmentation by integrating all accommodation processes into one platform:

User Role	Key Capabilities
Visitor / Prospective Tenant	Search, filter, map view, book viewings, submit applications, FAQ chatbot
Tenant	Tenant dashboard, lease signing, payment upload, maintenance requests, complaints, announcements
Admin	Property/room management, application review, smart allocation, payment verification, reporting dashboard

Design Patterns
1. Strategy Pattern (Notification System)
Purpose: Decouple notification logic from delivery mechanisms.

Implementation:

text
INotificationStrategy (interface)
    ├── EmailNotificationStrategy
    ├── SMSNotificationStrategy
    └── InAppNotificationStrategy

INotificationManager (context)
    └── Iterates strategies and sends via all channels
Instance Interaction:

ViewingService calls notificationManager.notifyTenant(tenant, "Viewing confirmed")

NotificationManager iterates strategies list

Each strategy sends via its channel

2. Observer Pattern (Automated Vacancy Tracking)
Purpose: Auto-update dependent modules when state changes occur.

Implementation:

text
LeaseService (Subject)
    ├── registerObserver(obs)
    ├── unregisterObserver(obs)
    └── moveOutTenant(tenantId) → notifies all

IStatusObserver (Observer)
    ├── RoomStatusUpdater
    ├── ReportService
    └── AdminDashboard
Instance Interaction:

Admin triggers LeaseService.moveOutTenant(tenantId)

Service changes state and notifies all registered observers

Each observer receives update(tenantId, "MOVE_OUT")

Room status → Available, reports update, dashboard recalculates

3. Façade Pattern (Tenant Dashboard)
Purpose: Provide unified interface to complex subsystems.

Implementation:

text
TenantDashboardFacade
    ├── PaymentService
    ├── LeaseService
    ├── MaintenanceService
    └── AnnouncementsService

getDashboardData(userId) → consolidated DTO
4. Repository Pattern
Purpose: Abstract data access logic.

text
IRepository<T>
    ├── GetById(id)
    ├── GetAll()
    ├── Add(entity)
    ├── Update(entity)
    └── Delete(id)

Repository<T> : IRepository<T>
    └── Uses UniCribzDbContext
Database Schema
Entity Relationship Overview
Entity	Purpose	Key Relationships
User	All people (Visitor, Tenant, Admin) distinguished by role	→ University, → Tenant profile
University	Reference table for universities	← User, ← Application
Property	Unicribz house/building	→ Property_Image, → Room, ↔ Amenity
Property_Image	Gallery images for properties	← Property
Amenity	Reusable facilities (Wi-Fi, parking)	↔ Property (M:N)
Room	Individual bookable unit	← Property, → Lease, → Application
Application	Formal accommodation request	→ User, → Property, → Application_Document
Application_Document	Supporting docs (ID, registration)	← Application
Viewing	Scheduled property visit	→ User, → Property
Lease	Formal tenancy agreement	→ Tenant, → Room, → Payment
Payment	Rental charge and settlement	← Lease
Maintenance_Request	Tenant-reported issue	→ Tenant, → Room, → Maintenance_Photo
Maintenance_Photo	Photo evidence	← Maintenance_Request
Complaint	Non-maintenance concern	→ Tenant
Announcement	One-way communication	→ Property (optional)
Notification	Discrete alert	→ User
Document	Stored file in tenant record	→ Tenant
InventoryItem	Physical resources	→ Property, → Room
Status Enums
Maintenance Request Status:

text
Submitted → Assigned → InProgress → Completed
                ↑           ↓
                └── OnHold ─┘
                ↑
           Reopened (from Completed)
Room Status:

text
Available ⇄ Reserved → Occupied → UnderMaintenance
    ↑                       ↓            │
    └───────────────────────┘            │
    └────────────────────────────────────┘
Application Status:

text
Submitted → UnderReview → Approved → RoomAllocated
                       ↘ Rejected
Payment Status:

text
Pending → Verified → Paid
       ↘ Failed
Complaint Status:

text
Submitted → UnderReview → Resolved

Installation & Configuration
Step 1: Clone the Repository
bash
git clone https://github.com/SiyandaNduze/UniCribz-Student-Accommodation-System.git
cd UniCribz-Student-Accommodation-System
Step 2: Restore Dependencies
bash
dotnet restore
Step 3: Set Up the Database
bash
# Navigate to the Data project
cd src/UniCribz.Data

# Create initial migration (if not exists)
dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate --startup-project ../UniCribz.Api

# Apply migration to database
dotnet ef database update --startup-project ../UniCribz.Api
Step 4: Configure User Secrets (Development)
bash
cd src/UniCribz.Api
dotnet user-secrets init
dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection" "Host=localhost;..."
dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:Key" "YourSuperSecretKey..."
dotnet user-secrets set "GoogleMaps:ApiKey" "YourApiKey"
# ... set all other secrets
Step 5: Build the Solution
bash
dotnet build
Step 6: Run the Application
Option A: Run API and Web separately

bash
# Terminal 1 - API
cd src/UniCribz.Api
dotnet run

# Terminal 2 - Web
cd src/UniCribz.Web
dotnet run
Option B: Run with Docker Compose

bash
docker-compose up -d
Step 7: Verify Installation
API Swagger: https://localhost:5001/swagger

Web Frontend: https://localhost:5000

Health Check: https://localhost:5001/health

Running the Application

Health Check	https://localhost:5001/health

⚠️ Change all default passwords immediately in production!

Git Workflow & Branching Strategy
Branch Structure
text
main                    ← Production-ready, tagged releases only
├── develop             ← Integration branch, auto-deploys to Staging
│   ├── feature/booking-viewing
│   ├── feature/payment-verification
│   ├── feature/maintenance-tracking
│   └── feature/admin-dashboard
├── release/1.2.0       ← QA sign-off before merging to main
└── hotfix/1.2.1        ← Emergency production patches
Branch Protection Rules
Branch	Rules
main	Require PR, 1 approval, all CI checks pass, no direct pushes
develop	Require PR, 1 approval, all CI checks pass
Development Flow
bash
# 1. Create feature branch from develop
git checkout develop
git pull origin develop
git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name

# 2. Make changes and commit
git add .
git commit -m "feat: add property search filtering"

# 3. Push and open PR
git push origin feature/your-feature-name
# Open PR on GitHub into develop

# 4. After approval and CI pass, squash-merge into develop

# 5. For release:
git checkout -b release/1.0.0 develop
# Bump version, update changelog
# Open PR into main
# After QA sign-off and merge, tag:
git tag v1.0.0
git push origin v1.0.0
Commit Convention
text
feat:     New feature
fix:      Bug fix
docs:     Documentation
style:    Formatting
refactor: Code restructuring
test:     Adding tests
chore:    Maintenance
CI/CD Pipeline
GitHub Actions Workflows
1. ci.yml — Continuous Integration
Trigger: Push to feature/*, PR to develop

Jobs:

Lint & Static Analysis — ESLint, Flake8, .NET analyzers

Unit Tests — xUnit with coverage report

Build — Compile app, create Docker image

Integration Tests — API vs. ephemeral test DB

yaml
name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches: [ 'feature/**' ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ develop ]

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: '8.0.x'
      - run: dotnet format --verify-no-changes

  test:
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:15
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
      - run: dotnet test --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3

  build:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
      - run: dotnet publish -c Release -o ./publish
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: app-artifact
          path: ./publish
2. deploy-staging.yml — Staging Deployment
Trigger: Push to develop

yaml
name: Deploy to Staging
on:
  push:
    branches: [ develop ]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
      - run: dotnet publish -c Release -o ./publish
      - name: Deploy to Azure Staging
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: unicribz-staging
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZURE_STAGING_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}
          package: ./publish
      - name: Run Smoke Tests
        run: |
          # Playwright smoke tests against staging URL
3. deploy-production.yml — Production Deployment
Trigger: Tag push (e.g., v1.0.0)

yaml
name: Deploy to Production
on:
  push:
    tags: [ 'v*.*.*' ]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
      - run: dotnet publish -c Release -o ./publish
      - name: Deploy to Green Environment
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: unicribz-green
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZURE_PROD_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}
          package: ./publish
      - name: Health Check
        run: |
          curl -f https://unicribz-green.azurewebsites.net/health || exit 1
      - name: Switch Traffic to Green
        run: |
          az webapp traffic-routing set --name unicribz-prod --resource-group unicribz-rg --distribution green=100
Rollback Criteria
Error rate > 5% over 5-minute window

Response time > 3 seconds over 5-minute window

Critical security vulnerability discovered

Critical user-reported bugs

Deployment Plan
Phase 1: Environment Setup
Create Azure Resource Groups for Dev, Staging, Production

Deploy VNet with 3 subnets (Public, Private, Protected)

Configure NSGs with strict inbound/outbound rules

Deploy PostgreSQL Flexible Server (HA enabled for Staging/Prod)

Deploy Azure Cache for Redis

Create Blob Storage containers

Deploy VMSS for Presentation and Application tiers with auto-scaling

Deploy Application Gateway with WAF

Phase 2: Application Build & Artifact Generation
Commit code to main branch

CI pipeline triggers automatically

Frontend: Install deps → Build → Test

Backend: Restore → Compile → Test → Publish

Publish artifacts to Azure DevOps Artifacts

Phase 3: Pre-Deployment Validation
Deploy to Staging environment

Run automated smoke tests

Run performance/load tests

Manual QA validation

Security vulnerability scan

Phase 4: Deployment to Production (Blue-Green)
Blue = current live version, Green = new version

Deploy new version to Green environment

Run health checks on Green

Switch Application Gateway traffic from Blue to Green

Monitor Green environment

Phase 5: Post-Deployment Verification & Rollback
Run final automated + manual tests

Monitor Application Insights metrics

Rollback: Switch traffic back to Blue if issues detected

Decommission Blue after successful period

Rollout Strategy
Phase	Environment	Method	Audience	Duration
1	Development	Auto on commit	Dev Team	Continuous
2	Staging	Auto on Dev build	QA Team	24–48 hrs
3	Production (Canary)	Manual approval	5–10% users	1–2 hrs
4	Production (Full)	Manual approval	All users	N/A
Security Architecture
Security Principles
Least Privilege: Only necessary permissions granted

Defence in Depth: Multiple security layers

Secure by Default: Secure defaults, minimal public endpoints

Fail Secure: Deny access on control failure

Separation of Duties: Payment verification separate from tenant management

Auditability: All security events logged in Azure Monitor

Network Security
Layer	Controls
VNet Isolation	3 segregated subnets
NSGs	Strict inbound/outbound rules per subnet
Application Gateway + WAF	OWASP Core Rule Set 3.2, SSL termination
Azure DDoS Protection	Volumetric + state-exhaustion protection
NAT Gateway	Predictable outbound source IP
Private Endpoints	PostgreSQL and Redis removed from public internet
Application Security
Threat	Mitigation
XSS	Input validation, output encoding, CSP headers, WAF rules
SQL Injection	Parameterized queries (EF Core), WAF rules, least privilege DB access
CSRF	Anti-CSRF tokens, SameSite cookies, idempotent operations
Account Compromise	MFA for admins, strong password policy, account lockout (5 attempts)
Session Hijacking	Short-lived JWT, HTTP-only + SameSite cookies, refresh tokens
Insecure File Uploads	File type/size validation, malware scanning, randomized names
MITM	TLS 1.2+ enforced everywhere
Vulnerable Dependencies	OWASP Dependency Check, automated updates
Data Security
Encryption at Rest: Azure SSE for PostgreSQL and Blob Storage

Encryption in Transit: TLS 1.2+ for all communications

Data Masking: Sensitive data masked in UI/logs

Data Minimisation: Only required data collected

Secure Backup: Encrypted, restricted access, separate storage account

Data Retention: Tenant data retained 5 years post-move-out, then anonymized/deleted

Identity & Access Management
Azure AD (Entra ID) for admin accounts with conditional access

Managed Identities for application-to-Azure-service auth

RBAC with 3 roles: Visitor, Tenant, Admin

Audit Logging of all auth events to Azure Monitor

Compliance
POPIA (South Africa): Right to access, correct, delete personal data

Data Retention Policies: Clear lifecycle management

Security Monitoring: Azure Security Center + Sentinel SIEM

Non-Functional Requirements
Category	Requirement
Performance	API response < 500ms (p95), page load < 3s
Scalability	Auto-scale VMSS based on CPU/request count
Availability	99.9% uptime SLA
Security	RBAC, MFA, encryption, OWASP Top 10 protections
Maintainability	Coding standards, version control, automated tests
Usability	Application completion within 10 minutes
Interoperability	Google Maps API integration, payment gateway
Compatibility	Latest Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari; mobile responsive
Accessibility	WCAG 2.1 AA, screen reader support, readable text

Cost Optimisation Strategies
Auto-Scaling: VMSS scales in during off-peak (20–30% savings)

Burstable VMs (B-Series): Cheapest tier (60–80% vs D-Series)

Free Tiers: Blob Storage (5GB), Azure AD (50K objects)

Right-Sizing: Regular review based on actual usage (20–40% savings)

Basic Redis: Cheapest tier (~$16/month)

Reserved Instances: Reassess at Year 1 for stable workloads

Change Management & Handover
ADKAR Model
Stage	Approach
Awareness	Management briefings, staff meetings, email/social media for students
Desire	Show what's in it for admins (less manual work) and students (transparency)
Knowledge	Hands-on training in real workflows
Ability	Train-the-trainer workshops, in-app onboarding
Reinforcement	Support, feedback loops, habit forming
Training Plan
Audience	Approach
Admin Staff	Half-day hands-on train-the-trainer workshop; internal champions
Tenants/Students	Short video guides (2–3 min) embedded in portal; onboarding tooltips; FAQ chatbot
Visitors	No training needed — intuitive self-service UI validated via UAT
Migration & Cutover
Data Migration: Extract from spreadsheets → clean → map → load to staging DB for validation

Parallel Run (Pilot): One property runs both old and new systems for 2 weeks

Full Cutover: Remaining properties migrated in a single scheduled weekend window

Fallback Window: Legacy system read-only for 30 days post-go-live

Support Strategy
Phase	Approach
Hypercare (Weeks 1–2)	Same-day response, daily check-ins
Steady State (Week 3+)	Tier 1: Admin champions + chatbot; Tier 2: Dev team; Tier 3: Infrastructure
Continuous Feedback	In-app feedback + monthly ticket/usage review
Success Criteria
Adoption: 80% of active tenants log in within 30 days

Operational: Measurable reduction in admin reconciliation time

Reliability: Uptime/response targets met, zero critical incidents by Week 2

Testing Strategy
Test Pyramid
text
         ┌─────────────┐
         │   E2E Tests │  (Playwright) — Critical user journeys
         │    ~10%     │
         ├─────────────┤
         │ Integration │  (WebApplicationFactory + Testcontainers)
         │    ~30%     │
         ├─────────────┤
         │  Unit Tests │  (xUnit + Moq) — Business logic
         │    ~60%     │
         └─────────────┘
Unit Tests
Focus: Individual methods, services, business logic

Examples:

SmartAllocationService ranking logic

NotificationManager strategy iteration

Room.reserve() status transitions

Application.approve() workflow

Run:

bash
dotnet test tests/UniCribz.Api.Tests
Integration Tests
Focus: API endpoints, database queries, validation

Setup: Testcontainers for PostgreSQL and Redis

Run:

bash
dotnet test tests/UniCribz.Api.Tests/IntegrationTests
E2E Tests (Playwright)
Focus: Complete user workflows through the UI

Critical Journeys:

Visitor searches → books viewing → submits application

Admin approves application → allocates room → creates lease

Tenant signs lease → uploads payment → submits maintenance

Admin assigns maintenance → updates status → completes

Run:

bash
cd tests/UniCribz.E2E.Tests
dotnet test
Load Tests
Tool: k6 or Azure Load Testing

1,000 concurrent users browsing properties

100 concurrent applications submitting

50 concurrent admin operations

Troubleshooting
Common Issues
Issue	Cause	Solution
dotnet ef not found	EF Core tools not installed	dotnet tool install --global dotnet-ef
Database connection failed	PostgreSQL not running	Check Docker container / service
JWT 401 Unauthorized	Invalid/expired token	Re-login, check token expiry
Redis connection failed	Redis not running	docker start unicribz-redis
CORS errors	Frontend URL not in CORS policy	Update Program.cs CORS config
Google Maps not loading	Invalid API key	Check appsettings.json / user secrets
Migration fails	Pending model changes	dotnet ef migrations add <name>
Blob upload fails	Invalid connection string	Verify Azure Storage credentials
Email not sending	SendGrid API key invalid	Check SendGrid dashboard
SMS not sending	Twilio credentials invalid	Check Twilio console
Logs
Environment	Location
Development	Console + Visual Studio Output
Staging	Azure Application Insights
Production	Azure Application Insights + Azure Monitor

5.7 Dockerfile
Create Dockerfile in the root:

dockerfile
# Build stage
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

COPY ["src/UniCribz.Api/UniCribz.Api.csproj", "src/UniCribz.Api/"]
COPY ["src/UniCribz.Data/UniCribz.Data.csproj", "src/UniCribz.Data/"]
COPY ["src/UniCribz.Shared/UniCribz.Shared.csproj", "src/UniCribz.Shared/"]
RUN dotnet restore "src/UniCribz.Api/UniCribz.Api.csproj"

COPY . .
WORKDIR "/src/src/UniCribz.Api"
RUN dotnet build "UniCribz.Api.csproj" -c Release -o /app/build

# Publish stage
FROM build AS publish
RUN dotnet publish "UniCribz.Api.csproj" -c Release -o /app/publish /p:UseAppHost=false

# Runtime stage
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0 AS final
WORKDIR /app
EXPOSE 8080
EXPOSE 8081
COPY --from=publish /app/publish .
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "UniCribz.Api.dll"]
⚙️ Step 6: Configure the Backend API
6.1 Update src/UniCribz.Api/Program.cs
Replace the entire contents of Program.cs:

csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens;
using Microsoft.OpenApi.Models;
using Serilog;
using System.Text;
using UniCribz.Data.Context;
using UniCribz.Api.Extensions;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Serilog
Log.Logger = new LoggerConfiguration()
    .ReadFrom.Configuration(builder.Configuration)
    .Enrich.FromLogContext()
    .WriteTo.Console()
    .CreateLogger();

builder.Host.UseSerilog();

// Database
builder.Services.AddDbContext<UniCribzDbContext>(options =>
    options.UseNpgsql(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection")));

// Redis Cache
builder.Services.AddStackExchangeRedisCache(options =>
{
    options.Configuration = builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Redis");
    options.InstanceName = "UniCribz_";
});

// JWT Authentication
var jwtKey = builder.Configuration["Jwt:Key"] ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("JWT Key not configured");
builder.Services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
    .AddJwtBearer(options =>
    {
        options.TokenValidationParameters = new TokenValidationParameters
        {
            ValidateIssuer = true,
            ValidateAudience = true,
            ValidateLifetime = true,
            ValidateIssuerSigningKey = true,
            ValidIssuer = builder.Configuration["Jwt:Issuer"],
            ValidAudience = builder.Configuration["Jwt:Audience"],
            IssuerSigningKey = new SymmetricSecurityKey(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(jwtKey))
        };
    });

builder.Services.AddAuthorization(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("AdminOnly", policy => policy.RequireRole("Admin"));
    options.AddPolicy("TenantOnly", policy => policy.RequireRole("Tenant"));
    options.AddPolicy("TenantOrAdmin", policy => policy.RequireRole("Tenant", "Admin"));
});

// CORS
builder.Services.AddCors(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("AllowWebApp", policy =>
    {
        policy.WithOrigins(
                builder.Configuration["App:WebBaseUrl"] ?? "https://localhost:5000")
              .AllowAnyHeader()
              .AllowAnyMethod()
              .AllowCredentials();
    });
});

// Application Services (each member will add their services here)
builder.Services.AddApplicationServices();

// Controllers & API
builder.Services.AddControllers();
builder.Services.AddEndpointsApiExplorer();

// Swagger
builder.Services.AddSwaggerGen(c =>
{
    c.SwaggerDoc("v1", new OpenApiInfo
    {
        Title = "UniCribz API",
        Version = "v1",
        Description = "Student Accommodation Management System API"
    });
    c.AddSecurityDefinition("Bearer", new OpenApiSecurityScheme
    {
        Description = "JWT Authorization header using the Bearer scheme.",
        Name = "Authorization",
        In = ParameterLocation.Header,
        Type = SecuritySchemeType.ApiKey,
        Scheme = "Bearer"
    });
    c.AddSecurityRequirement(new OpenApiSecurityRequirement
    {
        {
            new OpenApiSecurityScheme
            {
                Reference = new OpenApiReference
                {
                    Type = ReferenceType.SecurityScheme,
                    Id = "Bearer"
                }
            },
            Array.Empty<string>()
        }
    });
});

// Health Checks
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()
    .AddNpgSql(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection")!)
    .AddRedis(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Redis")!);

var app = builder.Build();

// Middleware pipeline
if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.UseSwagger();
    app.UseSwaggerUI();
}

app.UseSerilogRequestLogging();
app.UseHttpsRedirection();
app.UseCors("AllowWebApp");
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();
app.MapControllers();
app.MapHealthChecks("/health");

app.Run();

csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews();
builder.Services.AddHttpClient("UniCribzApi", client =>
{
    client.BaseAddress = new Uri(builder.Configuration["Api:BaseUrl"] ?? "https://localhost:5001");
});
builder.Services.AddSession(options =>
{
    options.IdleTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30);
    options.Cookie.HttpOnly = true;
    options.Cookie.IsEssential = true;
});

var app = builder.Build();

if (!app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.UseExceptionHandler("/Home/Error");
    app.UseHsts();
}

app.UseHttpsRedirection();
app.UseStaticFiles();
app.UseRouting();
app.UseSession();
app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapControllerRoute(
    name: "default",
    pattern: "{controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}");

app.Run();

🔄 Step 10: Set Up GitHub Actions CI/CD
10.1 Create .github/workflows/ci.yml
yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ 'feature/**' ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ develop, main ]

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint & Static Analysis
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: '8.0.x'
      - name: Restore
        run: dotnet restore
      - name: Format check
        run: dotnet format --verify-no-changes --verbosity diagnostic

  test:
    name: Unit Tests
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:15
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: UniCribzTestDb
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      redis:
        image: redis:7
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: '8.0.x'
      - name: Restore
        run: dotnet restore
      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build --no-restore -c Release
      - name: Test
        run: dotnet test --no-build -c Release --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"
      - name: Upload coverage
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  build:
    name: Build Artifact
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: '8.0.x'
      - name: Publish API
        run: dotnet publish src/UniCribz.Api/UniCribz.Api.csproj -c Release -o ./publish/api
      - name: Publish Web
        run: dotnet publish src/UniCribz.Web/UniCribz.Web.csproj -c Release -o ./publish/web
      - name: Upload API artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: api-artifact
          path: ./publish/api
      - name: Upload Web artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: web-artifact
          path: ./publish/web

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4

          dotnet-version: '8.0.x'

      - name: Deploy to Green slot
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: 'unicribz-api'
          slot-name: 'green'
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZURE_PROD_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}

      - name: Health check on Green
        run: curl -f https://unicribz-api-green.azurewebsites.net/health || exit 1
      - name: Swap slots
        uses: azure/CLI@v2
        with:
          inlineScript: |
            az webapp deployment slot swap --name unicribz-api --resource-group unicribz-rg --slot green --target-slot production

when i run this: dotnet --version i get 10.*
The user says when they run dotnet --version they get 10.*. This means they have .NET 10 SDK installed instead of .NET 8. This is a problem because the project targets .NET 8. I need to help them fix this.

.NET 10 is quite new (released November 2025 presumably, based on the context of the conversation being in 2026). .NET 8 is the LTS version they want to target.

Options:

Install .NET 8 SDK alongside .NET 10 (side-by-side installation is supported)

Use global.json to pin to .NET 8

Change the project to target .NET 10 instead

The best approach is to install .NET 8 SDK side-by-side and use global.json to pin the version. This way they keep both.

Let me write clear instructions.

🔧 Fix: Pinning the Project to .NET 8
You have .NET 10 SDK installed, but the UniCribz project targets .NET 8 LTS. This is a common situation — you can run both SDKs side-by-side. Since .NET 8 is the Long-Term Support (LTS) release and matches the project document, we'll pin the project to .NET 8.

You have two options — pick one:

✅ Option A (Recommended): Install .NET 8 SDK Side-by-Side
.NET SDKs are designed to be installed side-by-side, so .NET 10 and .NET 8 can coexist without conflict.

Step 1: Install .NET 8 SDK
Go to: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0

Under .NET 8.0 → SDK → download the x64 installer for Windows

Run the installer (default options are fine)

Close and reopen all terminals and Visual Studio

Step 2: Verify both SDKs are installed
Open a new terminal and run:

bash
dotnet --list-sdks
You should now see both, for example:

text
8.0.404 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk]
10.0.100 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk]
If you only see 10.*, the .NET 8 SDK install failed — retry Step 1.

Step 3: Pin the project to .NET 8 via global.json
Create a file called global.json in the repository root (same level as UniCribz.sln):

json
{
  "sdk": {
    "version": "8.0.0",
    "rollForward": "latestFeature",
    "allowPrerelease": false
  }
}
This tells the .NET CLI: "Always use the .NET 8 SDK in this folder and all subfolders, even if newer SDKs are installed."

Step 4: Verify the pin is working
From the repository root, run:

bash
dotnet --version
Expected output:

text
8.0.xxx
Now dotnet uses .NET 8 for this repo automatically. ✅

Step 5: Confirm the build still works
bash
dotnet restore
dotnet build
If both succeed, you're done. Continue with the setup guide from Step 4: Create the Complete Folder Structure.

⚙️ Option B: Target .NET 10 Instead (Not Recommended)
You could switch the whole project to .NET 10, but this is not recommended because:

❌ The project document specifies .NET 8 / modern JavaScript framework

❌ Most Azure deployment templates and third-party libraries are tested against .NET 8 LTS

❌ .NET 10 is not an LTS release (only odd-numbered versions like 9 are STS; 8 and 10 differ in support windows)

❌ Some NuGet packages listed in the dependency list may not yet have .NET 10 versions

If you still want to do this (e.g., if installing .NET 8 fails), change Directory.Build.props in the repo root:

xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
Then update global.json:

json
{
  "sdk": {
    "version": "10.0.0",
    "rollForward": "latestMinor"
  }
}
And update the Dockerfile — change every 8.0 to 10.0:

dockerfile
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build
...
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS final
But again — Option A is the correct path for this project.

🎯 Recommendation
Option A: Install .NET 8	Option B: Use .NET 10
Matches project doc	✅ Yes	❌ No

🚨 Why Your Multi-Line Paste Kept Breaking
Look at your terminal output:

text
PS C:\Users\siyan\Source\Repos\INSY7315-2026-MOTIVATION> pwd
>> Get-ChildItem
>> Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter "*.sln"
The >> prefix means PowerShell is stuck in "continuation mode" — it thinks the previous command wasn't finished. This happens when a pasted block contains:

An unclosed quote " or brace {

A | pipe at the end of a line with nothing after it

A backtick ` at the end of a line

When PowerShell enters continuation mode, your next commands become arguments to the broken previous command, and nothing actually runs.

Fix for the future:
Paste one command at a time — press Enter, wait for it to finish, then paste the next

If you see >> appear in your prompt, press Ctrl+C to cancel the broken command and return to a normal prompt PS ...>

Step 2: Update API Program.cs
Run this as one command to replace the default template:

powershell
$program = @'
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens;
using Microsoft.OpenApi.Models;
using Serilog;
using System.Text;
using UniCribz.Api.Extensions;
using UniCribz.Data.Context;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Serilog
Log.Logger = new LoggerConfiguration()
    .ReadFrom.Configuration(builder.Configuration)
    .Enrich.FromLogContext()
    .WriteTo.Console()
    .CreateLogger();
builder.Host.UseSerilog();

// Database
builder.Services.AddDbContext<UniCribzDbContext>(options =>
    options.UseNpgsql(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection")));

// Redis Cache
builder.Services.AddStackExchangeRedisCache(options =>
{
    options.Configuration = builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Redis");
    options.InstanceName = "UniCribz_";
});

// JWT Authentication
var jwtKey = builder.Configuration["Jwt:Key"] ?? "CHANGE_ME_IN_APPSETTINGS_AT_LEAST_32_CHARS_LONG!!";
builder.Services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
    .AddJwtBearer(options =>
    {
        options.TokenValidationParameters = new TokenValidationParameters
        {
            ValidateIssuer = true,
            ValidateAudience = true,
            ValidateLifetime = true,
            ValidateIssuerSigningKey = true,
            ValidIssuer = builder.Configuration["Jwt:Issuer"] ?? "UniCribz",
            ValidAudience = builder.Configuration["Jwt:Audience"] ?? "UniCribzClients",
            IssuerSigningKey = new SymmetricSecurityKey(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(jwtKey))
        };
    });

builder.Services.AddAuthorization(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("AdminOnly", policy => policy.RequireRole("Admin"));
    options.AddPolicy("TenantOnly", policy => policy.RequireRole("Tenant"));
    options.AddPolicy("TenantOrAdmin", policy => policy.RequireRole("Tenant", "Admin"));
});

// CORS
builder.Services.AddCors(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("AllowWebApp", policy =>
    {
        policy.WithOrigins(builder.Configuration["App:WebBaseUrl"] ?? "https://localhost:5000")
              .AllowAnyHeader()
              .AllowAnyMethod()
              .AllowCredentials();
    });
});

// Application Services
builder.Services.AddApplicationServices();

// Controllers & API
builder.Services.AddControllers();
builder.Services.AddEndpointsApiExplorer();

// Swagger
builder.Services.AddSwaggerGen(c =>
{
    c.SwaggerDoc("v1", new OpenApiInfo
    {
        Title = "UniCribz API",
        Version = "v1",
        Description = "Student Accommodation Management System API"
    });
    c.AddSecurityDefinition("Bearer", new OpenApiSecurityScheme
    {
        Description = "JWT Authorization header using the Bearer scheme.",
        Name = "Authorization",
        In = ParameterLocation.Header,
        Type = SecuritySchemeType.ApiKey,
        Scheme = "Bearer"
    });
    c.AddSecurityRequirement(new OpenApiSecurityRequirement
    {
        {
            new OpenApiSecurityScheme
            {
                Reference = new OpenApiReference { Type = ReferenceType.SecurityScheme, Id = "Bearer" }
            },
            Array.Empty<string>()
        }
    });
});

// Health Checks
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()
    .AddNpgSql(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection") ?? "")
    .AddRedis(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Redis") ?? "");

var app = builder.Build();

if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.UseSwagger();
    app.UseSwaggerUI();
}

app.UseSerilogRequestLogging();
app.UseHttpsRedirection();
app.UseCors("AllowWebApp");
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();
app.MapControllers();
app.MapHealthChecks("/health");

app.Run();
'@
Set-Content -Path "src/UniCribz.Api/Program.cs" -Value $program -Encoding UTF8
Write-Host "Program.cs (API) updated successfully." -ForegroundColor Green

# UniCribz Setup Scripts

These scripts automate the initial setup of the UniCribz repository. Run them after cloning to get your environment ready.

## Prerequisites

- .NET 8 SDK installed (`dotnet --version` should show `8.0.x`)
- Git installed
- PowerShell 5.1+ or PowerShell 7+
- (Optional) Docker Desktop for local PostgreSQL and Redis

## One-Command Setup

From the repository root:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup/00-run-all.ps1
This runs all scripts in the correct order and finishes with a build to verify everything works.

Individual Scripts
Run them one at a time if you prefer:

Script	Purpose
01-add-references.ps1	Wires up project references (API → Data, Data → Shared, etc.)
02-add-nuget-packages.ps1	Installs all NuGet dependencies
03-create-folders.ps1	Creates the full folder structure
Manual Override
If PowerShell blocks script execution:

powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass
Then re-run the script.

Verifying
After setup, run:

powershell
dotnet restore
dotnet build
dotnet test
All three should complete with 0 errors.

Troubleshooting
Issue	Fix
dotnet: command not found	Install .NET 8 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0
Unable to find package	Run dotnet nuget locals all --clear then retry
Script execution is disabled	Run Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass
Project does not exist	Make sure you are in the repository root
'@

📌 Why This Happened
C# namespaces are implicit — they exist only if at least one compiled type declares them. Earlier, the guide said to add:

csharp
using UniCribz.Api.Services;
using UniCribz.Api.Services.Interfaces;
using UniCribz.Api.Notifications;
at the top of ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs. Those usings assumed the folders contained .cs files declaring types — but they were empty. So the compiler reported:

text
The type or namespace name 'Services' does not exist in the namespace 'UniCribz.Api'
Removing the unused usings (Step 1) fixes it. The placeholder file (Step 2) is a convenience for future work.

function Write-NewFile {
    param([string]$Path, [string]$Content)
    if (Test-Path $Path) {
        Write-Host "  Skip: $Path" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        return
    }
    $dir = Split-Path -Parent $Path
    if ($dir -and -not (Test-Path $dir)) {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dir -Force | Out-Null
    }
    Set-Content -Path $Path -Value $Content -Encoding UTF8
    Write-Host "  + $Path" -ForegroundColor Green
}

function Write-File {
    param([string]$Path, [string]$Content)
    if (Test-Path $Path) {
        Write-Host "  . skip: $Path" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        return
    }
    $dir = Split-Path -Parent $Path

function Make-Class {
    param([string]$Path, [string]$Namespace, [string]$ClassName)
    $c = "namespace $Namespace;`n`npublic class $ClassName`n{`n    // TODO: Implement`n}`n"

    param([string]$Path, [string]$Namespace, [string]$InterfaceName)

    Write-File -Path $Path -Content $c
}

    param([string]$Path, [string]$Namespace, [string]$EnumName)

$script:made = 0
function New-File {
    param([string]$Path, [string]$Content)
    if (Test-Path $Path) { return }
    $dir = Split-Path -Parent $Path
    if ($dir -and -not (Test-Path $dir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dir -Force | Out-Null }
    Set-Content -Path $Path -Value $Content -Encoding UTF8
    $script:made++
    Write-Host "  + $Path" -ForegroundColor Green
}

Step 5: Set Up CI/CD Workflows
Create .github/workflows/ci.yml:

powershell
Set-Content -Path ".github/workflows/ci.yml" -Encoding UTF8 -Value @'
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ 'feature/**', 'develop' ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ develop, main ]

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:15
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: UniCribzTestDb
        ports: [ 5432:5432 ]
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: '8.0.x'
      - run: dotnet restore
      - run: dotnet build --no-restore -c Release
      - run: dotnet test --no-build -c Release --verbosity normal
'@

🔧 All 3 GitHub Workflows — Complete Setup
Run this one command from your repo root. It creates all three workflow files with the correct paths matching your repo.

Create All 3 Workflow Files
powershell
# Ensure folder exists
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path ".github/workflows" -Force | Out-Null

# ============================================================
# 1. ci.yml — Continuous Integration
# ============================================================
Set-Content -Path ".github/workflows/ci.yml" -Encoding UTF8 -Value @'
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ 'feature/**', 'develop', 'main' ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ develop, main ]

env:
  DOTNET_VERSION: '8.0.x'
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: true
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: true

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint & Static Analysis
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: ${{ env.DOTNET_VERSION }}

      - name: Restore dependencies
        run: dotnet restore UniCribz.sln

      - name: Check code formatting
        run: dotnet format UniCribz.sln --verify-no-changes --verbosity diagnostic
        continue-on-error: true

  test:
    name: Unit & Integration Tests
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:15
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: UniCribzTestDb
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

      redis:
        image: redis:7
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: ${{ env.DOTNET_VERSION }}

      - name: Restore dependencies
        run: dotnet restore UniCribz.sln

      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build UniCribz.sln --no-restore -c Release

      - name: Run tests
        env:
          ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection: "Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=UniCribzTestDb;Username=postgres;Password=postgres"
          ConnectionStrings__Redis: "localhost:6379"
        run: |
          dotnet test UniCribz.sln `
            --no-build `
            -c Release `
            --verbosity normal `
            --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage" `
            --results-directory ./TestResults

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          directory: ./TestResults
          fail_ci_if_error: false
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}

      - name: Upload test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: test-results
          path: ./TestResults
          retention-days: 7

  build:
    name: Build & Publish Artifacts
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: ${{ env.DOTNET_VERSION }}

      - name: Restore dependencies
        run: dotnet restore UniCribz.sln

      - name: Publish API
        run: |
          dotnet publish src/UniCribz.Api/UniCribz.Api.csproj `
            -c Release `
            -o ./publish/api `
            --no-restore

      - name: Publish Web
        run: |
          dotnet publish src/UniCribz.Web/UniCribz.Web.csproj `
            -c Release `
            -o ./publish/web `
            --no-restore

      - name: Upload API artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: api-artifact
          path: ./publish/api
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Upload Web artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: web-artifact
          path: ./publish/web
          retention-days: 7
'@
Write-Host "  ✓ .github/workflows/ci.yml" -ForegroundColor Green

name: Deploy to Staging

on:
  push:

  DOTNET_NOLOGO: true
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: true

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build for Staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup .NET

        with:
          dotnet-version: ${{ env.DOTNET_VERSION }}

      - name: Restore
        run: dotnet restore UniCribz.sln

      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build UniCribz.sln --no-restore -c Release

      - name: Publish API
        run: |
          dotnet publish src/UniCribz.Api/UniCribz.Api.csproj `
            -c Release `
            -o ./publish/api `
            --no-restore

      - name: Publish Web
        run: |
          dotnet publish src/UniCribz.Web/UniCribz.Web.csproj `
            -c Release `
            -o ./publish/web `
            --no-restore

      - name: Upload artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: staging-artifacts
          path: ./publish
          retention-days: 7

  deploy-api:
    name: Deploy API to Staging
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: staging
      url: https://unicribz-api-staging.azurewebsites.net

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Download artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: staging-artifacts
          path: ./publish

      - name: Deploy API to Azure App Service
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: 'unicribz-api-staging'
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZURE_STAGING_API_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}
          package: ./publish/api

      - name: Run smoke tests
        run: |
          echo "Running smoke tests against https://unicribz-api-staging.azurewebsites.net"
          curl -f https://unicribz-api-staging.azurewebsites.net/health || exit 1
          echo "Smoke tests passed"

  deploy-web:
    name: Deploy Web to Staging
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: staging
      url: https://unicribz-web-staging.azurewebsites.net

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Download artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: staging-artifacts
          path: ./publish

      - name: Deploy Web to Azure App Service
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: 'unicribz-web-staging'
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZURE_STAGING_WEB_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}
          package: ./publish/web
'@
Write-Host "  ✓ .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml" -ForegroundColor Green

Set-Content -Path ".github/workflows/deploy-production.yml" -Encoding UTF8 -Value @'
name: Deploy to Production

on:
  push:
    tags: [ 'v*.*.*' ]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Version to deploy (e.g., v1.0.0)'
        required: true

env:
  DOTNET_VERSION: '8.0.x'
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: true
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: true

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build Release Artifacts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: ${{ env.DOTNET_VERSION }}

      - name: Restore
        run: dotnet restore UniCribz.sln

      - name: Run tests (gate)
        env:
          ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection: "Host=localhost;Database=UniCribzTestDb;Username=postgres;Password=postgres"
          ConnectionStrings__Redis: "localhost:6379"
        run: |
          dotnet test UniCribz.sln -c Release --verbosity normal

      - name: Publish API
        run: |
          dotnet publish src/UniCribz.Api/UniCribz.Api.csproj `
            -c Release `
            -o ./publish/api `
            --no-restore

      - name: Publish Web
        run: |
          dotnet publish src/UniCribz.Web/UniCribz.Web.csproj `
            -c Release `
            -o ./publish/web `
            --no-restore

      - name: Upload artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: production-artifacts
          path: ./publish
          retention-days: 30

  deploy-green:
    name: Deploy to Green Slot
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://unicribz-api.azurewebsites.net

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Download artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: production-artifacts
          path: ./publish

      - name: Deploy API to Green slot
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: 'unicribz-api'
          slot-name: 'green'
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZURE_PROD_API_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}
          package: ./publish/api

      - name: Deploy Web to Green slot
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: 'unicribz-web'
          slot-name: 'green'
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZURE_PROD_WEB_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}
          package: ./publish/web

      - name: Wait for Green slot to warm up
        run: sleep 30

      - name: Health check Green API
        run: |
          curl -f https://unicribz-api-green.azurewebsites.net/health || exit 1
          echo "Green API is healthy"

  swap-slots:
    name: Swap Green to Production
    needs: deploy-green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://unicribz-api.azurewebsites.net

    steps:
      - name: Azure login
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Swap API slot
        uses: azure/CLI@v2
        with:
          inlineScript: |
            az webapp deployment slot swap \
              --name unicribz-api \
              --resource-group unicribz-rg \
              --slot green \
              --target-slot production

      - name: Swap Web slot
        uses: azure/CLI@v2
        with:
          inlineScript: |
            az webapp deployment slot swap \
              --name unicribz-web \
              --resource-group unicribz-rg \
              --slot green \
              --target-slot production

  verify:
    name: Post-Deploy Verification
    needs: swap-slots
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Health check Production API
        run: |
          for i in {1..5}; do
            if curl -f https://unicribz-api.azurewebsites.net/health; then
              echo "Production API is healthy"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "Attempt $i failed, retrying in 10s..."
            sleep 10
          done
          echo "Production health check failed — consider rollback"
          exit 1

  rollback:
    name: Rollback (if needed)
    needs: verify
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - name: Azure login
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Swap back to previous version
        uses: azure/CLI@v2
        with:
          inlineScript: |
            echo "ROLLING BACK"
            az webapp deployment slot swap \
              --name unicribz-api \
              --resource-group unicribz-rg \
              --slot production \
              --target-slot green
            az webapp deployment slot swap \
              --name unicribz-web \
              --resource-group unicribz-rg \
              --slot production \
              --target-slot green
'@
Write-Host "  ✓ .github/workflows/deploy-production.yml" -ForegroundColor Green

📋 What Each Workflow Does
1. ci.yml — Runs on Every Push & PR
Triggers:

Push to feature/**, develop, main

PR to develop or main

Jobs (in order):

Lint — Checks code formatting with dotnet format

Test — Spins up PostgreSQL + Redis containers, runs all tests, uploads coverage

Build — Publishes API + Web as artifacts

What teammates see: ✅ or ❌ on their PR. Cannot merge if red.

2. deploy-staging.yml — Auto-Deploy on Merge to develop
Triggers:

Push to develop (i.e., after a PR is merged)

Manual trigger from GitHub UI

Jobs:

Build — Compiles release version

Deploy API — Pushes to Azure App Service unicribz-api-staging

Deploy Web — Pushes to Azure App Service unicribz-web-staging

Smoke Test — Hits /health endpoint on staging

3. deploy-production.yml — Blue-Green Deploy on Tag
Triggers:

Push a version tag: git tag v1.0.0 && git push --tags

Manual trigger from GitHub UI

Jobs:

Build — Full test gate + release build

Deploy Green — Deploys to Azure staging slot "green"

Health Check — Verifies green is healthy

Swap Slots — Traffic switched from blue → green (zero downtime)

Verify — Post-deploy health checks on production

Rollback — If verify fails, automatically swaps back

🔐 GitHub Secrets Required (Later, When You Deploy)
You'll need to add these in GitHub repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions:

Secret	Purpose
AZURE_STAGING_API_PUBLISH_PROFILE	Azure App Service publish profile (API staging)
AZURE_STAGING_WEB_PUBLISH_PROFILE	Azure App Service publish profile (Web staging)
AZURE_PROD_API_PUBLISH_PROFILE	Azure App Service publish profile (API prod)
AZURE_PROD_WEB_PUBLISH_PROFILE	Azure App Service publish profile (Web prod)
AZURE_CREDENTIALS	Service principal JSON for az login
CODECOV_TOKEN (optional)	Codecov upload token
You don't need these yet — the CI workflow runs fine without them. Only add them when you actually deploy to Azure (later milestone).

🎯 Smart Question — Here's the Right Strategy
TL;DR
Push all 3 workflows now. They won't run on their own because:

deploy-staging.yml only triggers on push to develop (or manual)

deploy-production.yml only triggers on version tags (or manual)

Since you won't push to develop yet and won't create tags, they just sit there idle until you're ready. But having them in the repo:

✅ Shows your DevOps architecture to the lecturer (part of the module)

✅ Makes them ready the moment you have Azure set up

✅ Teammates can see the full deployment plan

✅ Zero risk — nothing runs accidentally

📅 Recommended Timeline
Phase	What You Do	Workflows Active
Now (Week 1)	Push all 3 workflows. Team starts coding on feature/* branches.	Only ci.yml runs
Week 2–3	Team merges features to develop.	ci.yml runs on PR + deploy-staging.yml skips (no Azure secrets)
Week 3–4	Set up Azure (see below) and add secrets.	Both deploy workflows become live
Week 4+	Tag v1.0.0 for submission.	Production workflow runs blue-green
⚠️ One Important Note About Pushing to develop
If you push the workflows to develop right now, the CI workflow will run. But deploy-staging.yml will also try to run on every push to develop — and it will fail because:

❌ AZURE_STAGING_API_PUBLISH_PROFILE secret doesn't exist

❌ Azure App Service unicribz-api-staging doesn't exist

That's fine — failed deployments don't break anything, but they clutter the Actions tab.

✅ Best Practice: Guard the Deploy Workflows
I'll give you an updated version of the two deploy workflows that only run if the secrets exist. This way you can push all 3 now without any red ❌ in your Actions tab.

🔧 Fix: Add Secret Guard to Both Deploy Workflows
Run this one command to update both deploy workflows so they skip gracefully when Azure isn't configured:

powershell
# ============================================================
# Recreate deploy-staging.yml with a guard
# ============================================================
Set-Content -Path ".github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml" -Encoding UTF8 -Value @'
name: Deploy to Staging

on:
  push:
    branches: [ develop ]
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  DOTNET_VERSION: '8.0.x'
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: true
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: true

jobs:
  # Check if Azure is configured
  check-azure:
    name: Check Azure Configuration
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      azure_ready: ${{ steps.check.outputs.ready }}
    steps:
      - id: check
        run: |
          if [ -n "${{ secrets.AZURE_STAGING_API_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}" ] && [ -n "${{ secrets.AZURE_STAGING_WEB_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}" ]; then
            echo "ready=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "✅ Azure staging is configured — proceeding with deployment"
          else
            echo "ready=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

Set-Content -Path ".github/workflows/deploy-production.yml" -Encoding UTF8 -Value @'
name: Deploy to Production

on:
  push:
    tags: [ 'v*.*.*' ]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Version to deploy (e.g., v1.0.0)'
        required: true

env:
  DOTNET_VERSION: '8.0.x'
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: true
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: true

jobs:
  check-azure:
    name: Check Azure Configuration
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      azure_ready: ${{ steps.check.outputs.ready }}
    steps:
      - id: check
        run: |
          if [ -n "${{ secrets.AZURE_PROD_API_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}" ] && [ -n "${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}" ]; then
            echo "ready=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "✅ Azure production is configured"
          else
            echo "ready=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "⏭️  Azure production not configured — skipping deployment"
          fi

  build:
    name: Build Release Artifacts
    needs: check-azure
    if: needs.check-azure.outputs.azure_ready == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: ${{ env.DOTNET_VERSION }}

      - name: Restore
        run: dotnet restore UniCribz.sln

      - name: Run tests (gate)
        run: dotnet test UniCribz.sln -c Release --verbosity normal

      - name: Publish API
        run: dotnet publish src/UniCribz.Api/UniCribz.Api.csproj -c Release -o ./publish/api --no-restore

      - name: Publish Web
        run: dotnet publish src/UniCribz.Web/UniCribz.Web.csproj -c Release -o ./publish/web --no-restore

      - name: Upload artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: production-artifacts
          path: ./publish
          retention-days: 30

  deploy-green:
    name: Deploy to Green Slot
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://unicribz-api.azurewebsites.net
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Download artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: production-artifacts
          path: ./publish

      - name: Deploy API to Green
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: 'unicribz-api'
          slot-name: 'green'
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZURE_PROD_API_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}
          package: ./publish/api

      - name: Deploy Web to Green
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: 'unicribz-web'
          slot-name: 'green'
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZURE_PROD_WEB_PUBLISH_PROFILE }}
          package: ./publish/web

      - name: Warm up Green slot
        run: sleep 30

      - name: Health check Green
        run: |
          curl -f https://unicribz-api-green.azurewebsites.net/health || exit 1

  swap-slots:
    name: Swap Green to Production
    needs: deploy-green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - name: Azure login
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Swap API slot
        uses: azure/CLI@v2
        with:
          inlineScript: |
            az webapp deployment slot swap --name unicribz-api --resource-group unicribz-rg --slot green --target-slot production

      - name: Swap Web slot
        uses: azure/CLI@v2
        with:
          inlineScript: |
            az webapp deployment slot swap --name unicribz-web --resource-group unicribz-rg --slot green --target-slot production

  verify:
    name: Post-Deploy Verification
    needs: swap-slots
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Health check Production API
        run: |
          for i in {1..5}; do
            if curl -f https://unicribz-api.azurewebsites.net/health; then
              echo "✅ Production healthy"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "Attempt $i failed, retrying..."
            sleep 10
          done
          exit 1

  rollback:
    name: Rollback (if needed)
    needs: verify
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - name: Azure login
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Swap back to previous version
        uses: azure/CLI@v2
        with:
          inlineScript: |
            echo "🔄 ROLLING BACK"
            az webapp deployment slot swap --name unicribz-api --resource-group unicribz-rg --slot production --target-slot green
            az webapp deployment slot swap --name unicribz-web --resource-group unicribz-rg --slot production --target-slot green
'@

1. Prerequisites (30 min)
bash

2. Create Resource Group
bash

3. Create App Services (Staging + Production)
bash
# Staging
