csharp
using System.Net;
using System.Text.Json;

namespace UniCribz.Api.Middleware;

public class ErrorHandlingMiddleware
{
    private readonly RequestDelegate _next;
    private readonly ILogger<ErrorHandlingMiddleware> _logger;
    private readonly IWebHostEnvironment _env;

    public ErrorHandlingMiddleware(
        RequestDelegate next,
        ILogger<ErrorHandlingMiddleware> logger,
        IWebHostEnvironment env)
    {
        _next = next;
        _logger = logger;
        _env = env;
    }

    public async Task InvokeAsync(HttpContext context)
    {
        try
        {
            await _next(context);
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            var correlationId = context.Items["X-Correlation-Id"]?.ToString();
            _logger.LogError(ex,
                "Unhandled exception for {Method} {Path} [CorrelationId={CorrelationId}]",
                context.Request.Method, context.Request.Path, correlationId);

            await WriteErrorAsync(context, ex, correlationId);
        }
    }

    private async Task WriteErrorAsync(HttpContext context, Exception ex, string? correlationId)
    {
        var (status, message) = ex switch
        {
            KeyNotFoundException => (HttpStatusCode.NotFound, ex.Message),
            UnauthorizedAccessException => (HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, ex.Message),
            InvalidOperationException => (HttpStatusCode.BadRequest, ex.Message),
            ArgumentException => (HttpStatusCode.BadRequest, ex.Message),
            _ => (HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError,
                  _env.IsDevelopment()
                    ? ex.Message
                    : "An unexpected error occurred. Please contact support with the correlation ID.")
        };

        context.Response.StatusCode = (int)status;
        context.Response.ContentType = "application/json";

        var payload = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new
        {
            error = message,
            statusCode = (int)status,
            correlationId,
            timestamp = DateTime.UtcNow
        });

        await context.Response.WriteAsync(payload);
    }
}

@'
namespace UniCribz.Api.Middleware;

public class SecurityHeadersMiddleware
{
    private readonly RequestDelegate _next;
    private readonly IWebHostEnvironment _env;

    public SecurityHeadersMiddleware(RequestDelegate next, IWebHostEnvironment env)
    {
        _next = next;
        _env = env;
    }

    public async Task InvokeAsync(HttpContext context)
    {
        var headers = context.Response.Headers;

        headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff";
        headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY";
        headers["X-XSS-Protection"] = "1; mode=block";
        headers["Referrer-Policy"] = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin";
        headers["Permissions-Policy"] = "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()";

        if (!_env.IsDevelopment())
        {
            headers["Content-Security-Policy"] =
                "default-src ''self''; " +
                "img-src ''self'' data: https:; " +
                "script-src ''self'' https://maps.googleapis.com; " +
                "style-src ''self'' ''unsafe-inline''; " +
                "font-src ''self'' data:; " +
                "connect-src ''self'' https://maps.googleapis.com; " +
                "frame-ancestors ''none''";
        }

        headers.Remove("X-Powered-By");
        headers.Remove("Server");

        await _next(context);
    }
}
'@ | Set-Content "src\UniCribz.Api\Middleware\SecurityHeadersMiddleware.cs" -Encoding UTF8
Write-Host "  [+] Middleware/SecurityHeadersMiddleware.cs" -ForegroundColor Green

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# File 5: Middleware/CorrelationIdMiddleware.cs
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
@'
namespace UniCribz.Api.Middleware;

public class CorrelationIdMiddleware
{
    private const string HeaderName = "X-Correlation-Id";
    private readonly RequestDelegate _next;
    private readonly ILogger<CorrelationIdMiddleware> _logger;

    public CorrelationIdMiddleware(RequestDelegate next, ILogger<CorrelationIdMiddleware> logger)
    {
        _next = next;
        _logger = logger;
    }

    public async Task InvokeAsync(HttpContext context)
    {
        var correlationId = context.Request.Headers[HeaderName].FirstOrDefault();

        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(correlationId))
            correlationId = Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N");

        context.Items[HeaderName] = correlationId;
        context.Response.Headers[HeaderName] = correlationId;
        context.TraceIdentifier = correlationId;

        using (_logger.BeginScope(new Dictionary<string, object>
        {
            ["CorrelationId"] = correlationId
        }))
        {
            await _next(context);
        }
    }
}
'@ | Set-Content "src\UniCribz.Api\Middleware\CorrelationIdMiddleware.cs" -Encoding UTF8
Write-Host "  [+] Middleware/CorrelationIdMiddleware.cs" -ForegroundColor Green

using UniCribz.Api.Options;

namespace UniCribz.Api.Extensions;

public static class ConfigurationExtensions
{
    public static IServiceCollection AddValidatedOptions(
        this IServiceCollection services,
        IConfiguration config)
    {
        services.AddOptions<JwtOptions>()
            .Bind(config.GetSection(JwtOptions.SectionName))
            .Validate(o => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(o.Key) && o.Key.Length >= 32,
                "Jwt:Key must be at least 32 characters.")
            .Validate(o => o.ExpiryMinutes > 0, "Jwt:ExpiryMinutes must be positive.")
            .ValidateOnStart();

        services.AddOptions<AppOptions>()
            .Bind(config.GetSection(AppOptions.SectionName))
            .Validate(o => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(o.WebBaseUrl),
                "App:WebBaseUrl is required.")
            .ValidateOnStart();

        services.AddOptions<DatabaseOptions>()
            .Bind(config.GetSection(DatabaseOptions.SectionName))
            .ValidateOnStart();

        return services;
    }
}

using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using UniCribz.Data.Context;

namespace UniCribz.Api.Extensions;

public static class WebApplicationExtensions
{
    public static async Task ApplyMigrationsAsync(this WebApplication app)
    {
        using var scope = app.Services.CreateScope();
        var db = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<UniCribzDbContext>();
        var logger = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<ILogger<Program>>();

        try
        {
            logger.LogInformation("Applying database migrations...");
            await db.Database.MigrateAsync();
            logger.LogInformation("Database migrations applied successfully.");
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            logger.LogCritical(ex, "Failed to apply database migrations.");
            throw;
        }
    }

    public static async Task SeedDatabaseAsync(this WebApplication app)
    {
        using var scope = app.Services.CreateScope();
        var db = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<UniCribzDbContext>();
        await DataSeeder.SeedAsync(db);
    }
}

csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HealthChecks;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.HttpOverrides;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.ResponseCompression;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks;
using Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens;
using Microsoft.OpenApi.Models;
using Serilog;
using Serilog.Events;
using System.Text;
using System.Threading.RateLimiting;
using UniCribz.Api.Extensions;
using UniCribz.Api.Middleware;
using UniCribz.Api.Options;
using UniCribz.Data.Context;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 1. LOGGING — Serilog (console + rolling file)
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Log.Logger = new LoggerConfiguration()
    .ReadFrom.Configuration(builder.Configuration)
    .Enrich.FromLogContext()
    .Enrich.WithMachineName()
    .Enrich.WithEnvironmentName()
    .Enrich.WithProperty("Application", "UniCribz.Api")
    .WriteTo.Console()
    .WriteTo.File(
        path: "logs/unicribz-.log",
        rollingInterval: RollingInterval.Day,
        retainedFileCountLimit: 30,
        restrictedToMinimumLevel: LogEventLevel.Information)
    .CreateLogger();

builder.Host.UseSerilog();

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 2. CONFIGURATION — validated options
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.AddValidatedOptions(builder.Configuration);

var jwtOptions = builder.Configuration.GetSection(JwtOptions.SectionName).Get<JwtOptions>()
                 ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Jwt configuration missing.");

var appOptions = builder.Configuration.GetSection(AppOptions.SectionName).Get<AppOptions>()
                 ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("App configuration missing.");

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 3. DATABASE — with retry
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.AddDbContext<UniCribzDbContext>(options =>
    options.UseNpgsql(
        builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection"),
        npgsql =>
        {
            npgsql.EnableRetryOnFailure(
                maxRetryCount: 3,
                maxRetryDelay: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5),
                errorCodesToAdd: null);
            npgsql.UseQuerySplittingBehavior(QuerySplittingBehavior.SplitQuery);
            npgsql.CommandTimeout(30);
        }));

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 4. CACHE
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.AddStackExchangeRedisCache(options =>
{
    options.Configuration = builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Redis");
    options.InstanceName = "UniCribz_";
});

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 5. AUTH
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
    .AddJwtBearer(options =>
    {
        options.TokenValidationParameters = new TokenValidationParameters
        {
            ValidateIssuer = true,
            ValidateAudience = true,
            ValidateLifetime = true,
            ValidateIssuerSigningKey = true,
            ValidIssuer = jwtOptions.Issuer,
            ValidAudience = jwtOptions.Audience,
            IssuerSigningKey = new SymmetricSecurityKey(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(jwtOptions.Key)),
            ClockSkew = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1)
        };
    });

builder.Services.AddAuthorization(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("AdminOnly", policy => policy.RequireRole("Admin"));
    options.AddPolicy("TenantOnly", policy => policy.RequireRole("Tenant"));
    options.AddPolicy("TenantOrAdmin", policy => policy.RequireRole("Tenant", "Admin"));
});

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 6. CORS
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.AddCors(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("AllowWebApp", policy =>
    {
        var origins = appOptions.AllowedOrigins.Length > 0
            ? appOptions.AllowedOrigins
            : new[] { appOptions.WebBaseUrl };

        policy.WithOrigins(origins)
              .AllowAnyHeader()
              .AllowAnyMethod()
              .AllowCredentials();
    });
});

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 7. RATE LIMITING
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.AddRateLimiter(options =>
{
    options.GlobalLimiter = PartitionedRateLimiter.Create<HttpContext, string>(context =>
    {
        var ip = context.Connection.RemoteIpAddress?.ToString() ?? "unknown";
        return RateLimitPartition.GetFixedWindowLimiter(
            partitionKey: ip,
            factory: _ => new FixedWindowRateLimiterOptions
            {
                PermitLimit = 100,
                Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1),
                QueueProcessingOrder = QueueProcessingOrder.OldestFirst,
                QueueLimit = 0
            });
    });
    options.RejectionStatusCode = StatusCodes.Status429TooManyRequests;
    options.OnRejected = async (context, token) =>
    {
        context.HttpContext.Response.Headers["Retry-After"] = "60";
        context.HttpContext.Response.ContentType = "application/json";
        await context.HttpContext.Response.WriteAsync(
            "{\"error\":\"Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.\",\"statusCode\":429}", token);
    };
});

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 8. RESPONSE COMPRESSION
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.AddResponseCompression(options =>
{
    options.EnableForHttps = true;
    options.Providers.Add<BrotliCompressionProvider>();
    options.Providers.Add<GzipCompressionProvider>();
});

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 9. FORWARDED HEADERS
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.Configure<ForwardedHeadersOptions>(options =>
{
    options.ForwardedHeaders = ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto;
    options.KnownNetworks.Clear();
    options.KnownProxies.Clear();
});

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 10. APPLICATION SERVICES + CONTROLLERS + SWAGGER
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.AddApplicationServices();
builder.Services.AddControllers();
builder.Services.AddEndpointsApiExplorer();

builder.Services.AddSwaggerGen(c =>
{
    c.SwaggerDoc("v1", new OpenApiInfo
    {
        Title = "UniCribz API",
        Version = "v1",
        Description = "Student Accommodation Management System API"
    });
    c.AddSecurityDefinition("Bearer", new OpenApiSecurityScheme
    {
        Description = "JWT Authorization header using the Bearer scheme.",
        Name = "Authorization",
        In = ParameterLocation.Header,
        Type = SecuritySchemeType.ApiKey,
        Scheme = "Bearer"
    });
    c.AddSecurityRequirement(new OpenApiSecurityRequirement
    {
        {
            new OpenApiSecurityScheme
            {
                Reference = new OpenApiReference { Type = ReferenceType.SecurityScheme, Id = "Bearer" }
            },
            Array.Empty<string>()
        }
    });
});

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 11. HEALTH CHECKS
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()
    .AddNpgSql(
        builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection")!,
        name: "postgresql",
        tags: new[] { "db", "ready" })
    .AddRedis(
        builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Redis")!,
        name: "redis",
        tags: new[] { "cache", "ready" })
    .AddCheck("self", () => HealthCheckResult.Healthy(), tags: new[] { "live" });

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 12. AUTOMAPPER
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
builder.Services.AddAutoMapper(typeof(UniCribz.Api.Mappings.MappingProfile));

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// BUILD
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// STARTUP TASKS
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
if (app.Configuration.GetValue<bool>("Database:MigrateOnStartup"))
    await app.ApplyMigrationsAsync();

if (app.Configuration.GetValue<bool>("Database:SeedOnStartup"))
    await app.SeedDatabaseAsync();

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// PIPELINE
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
app.UseForwardedHeaders();

if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment() || app.Environment.IsStaging())
{
    app.UseSwagger();
    app.UseSwaggerUI();
}

if (!app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.UseHsts();
}

app.UseHttpsRedirection();
app.UseMiddleware<SecurityHeadersMiddleware>();
app.UseMiddleware<CorrelationIdMiddleware>();
app.UseMiddleware<ErrorHandlingMiddleware>();
app.UseMiddleware<RequestLoggingMiddleware>();
app.UseResponseCompression();
app.UseCors("AllowWebApp");
app.UseRateLimiter();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();
app.MapControllers();

// Health checks
app.MapHealthChecks("/health");
app.MapHealthChecks("/health/live", new HealthCheckOptions
{
    Predicate = c => c.Tags.Contains("live"),
    ResponseWriter = async (context, report) =>
    {
        context.Response.ContentType = "application/json";
        await context.Response.WriteAsync("{\"status\":\"" + report.Status + "\"}");
    }
});
app.MapHealthChecks("/health/ready", new HealthCheckOptions
{
    Predicate = c => c.Tags.Contains("ready"),
    ResponseWriter = async (context, report) =>
    {
        context.Response.ContentType = "application/json";
        var checks = report.Entries.Select(e =>
            "\"" + e.Key + "\":\"" + e.Value.Status + "\"");
        await context.Response.WriteAsync(
            "{\"status\":\"" + report.Status + "\",\"checks\":{" +
            string.Join(",", checks) + "}}");
    }
});

app.Run();

Why It's Safe to Keep

No DI conflicts. You didn't register it in ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs, so nothing injects it.

No pipeline conflicts. Since Program.cs no longer calls UseMiddleware<RateLimitingMiddleware>(), it never runs.

The only real change is: your /api/... requests now flow through the framework's built-in limiter, not your custom one.

Recommendation — Keep It, But Mark It
For an assessment project, keeping it is actually a good idea:

It's documentation of your learning journey — you implemented a custom rate limiter first, then replaced it with the framework's built-in one. That's a story worth telling in your project defense.

Your lecturer may ask "how did you implement rate limiting?" — you can say "I wrote a custom one first (see LegacyRateLimitingMiddleware.cs), then replaced it with ASP.NET Core's built-in RateLimiter for better partitioning and sliding-window support."

It shows you understand both approaches, not just "I called a library."

So keep it, and add a small comment at the top so future-you (and the marker) understands why it's not wired up.

Rename + annotate

// LEGACY — Superseded by ASP.NET Core's built-in RateLimiter
//

// that informed the final decision.
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

NotificationManager.cs

csharp
public class NotificationManager : INotificationManager
{
    private readonly IEnumerable<INotificationStrategy> _strategies;
    public NotificationManager(IEnumerable<INotificationStrategy> strategies) => _strategies = strategies;

    public async Task NotifyAsync(string recipient, string message)
    {
        foreach (var strategy in _strategies)
            await strategy.SendAsync(recipient, message);
    }
}
Register in ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs

csharp
services.AddScoped<INotificationStrategy, EmailNotificationStrategy>();
services.AddScoped<INotificationStrategy, SMSNotificationStrategy>();
services.AddScoped<INotificationStrategy, InAppNotificationStrategy>();
services.AddScoped<INotificationManager, NotificationManager>();

public async Task<GeocodeResponse?> GeocodeAsync(string address)
{
    var client = new RestClient("https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json");
    var request = new RestRequest();
    request.AddQueryParameter("address", address);
    request.AddQueryParameter("key", _config["GoogleMaps:ApiKey"]);

    var response = await client.GetAsync<GeocodeResponse>(request);
    // parse lat/lng, return
}

⚠️ Important Things Sam Should Know
1. Docker Desktop Must Be Running
If you see Cannot connect to the Docker daemon, open Docker Desktop and wait for it to fully start. This is the #1 cause of "nothing works."

2. The API URL in appsettings.json Is http://localhost:5125
Not HTTPS. Not port 5001. Check src/UniCribz.Web/appsettings.json:

json
{
  "Api": {
    "BaseUrl": "http://localhost:5125"
  }
}
3. Rate Limiting — 100 Requests Per Minute Per IP
If your frontend fires too many requests during development (e.g., a loop on page load), you'll get:

json
{ "error": "Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.", "statusCode": 429 }
Wait 60 seconds and it resets. To avoid this during development, throttle your API calls (debounce search inputs, cache responses).

4. Correlation ID Header on Every Response
Every response includes X-Correlation-Id. If you need to debug an issue, grab that header and send it to Siyanda — he can search the API logs for that exact request.

5. Error Response Shape
All API errors come back as:

json
{
  "error": "Human-readable message",
  "statusCode": 400,
  "correlationId": "abc123...",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-02T10:30:00Z"
}
Handle this shape in your JavaScript.

6. The API Must Be Running Before the Web App Can Call It
If you get connection refused errors in your browser console, check Terminal 2 — is dotnet run still running?

🧰 If Something Breaks — Quick Fixes
Symptom	Fix
Cannot connect to Docker daemon	Open Docker Desktop, wait 30s, retry
Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1:5432	Postgres not running → docker-compose up -d
Now listening on doesn't appear	Port in use → restart VS/terminal
HTTPS certificate not trusted	dotnet dev-certs https --trust
429 Too Many Requests	Rate limit hit — wait 60 seconds
Web app loads but API calls fail	Check Api:BaseUrl in appsettings.json
Web app loads but shows blank	Press F12 → check Console for JS errors
dotnet build fails	dotnet clean && dotnet restore && dotnet build
Swagger shows "Unable to render"	Delete bin/ and obj/, rebuild
Can't log in as admin	Check /health/ready returns Healthy → if not, restart Docker

🏗️ Part 1: Environment Variables (Set Once)
Set these variables in PowerShell. They'll be reused throughout.

powershell
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Change these to your own values
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
$RESOURCE_GROUP       = "unicribz-rg"
$LOCATION             = "southafricanorth"     # closest to SA
$APP_SERVICE_PLAN     = "unicribz-plan"
$API_APP_NAME         = "unicribz-api"         # MUST be globally unique
$WEB_APP_NAME         = "unicribz-web"         # MUST be globally unique
$POSTGRES_SERVER      = "unicribz-db"          # MUST be globally unique
$POSTGRES_ADMIN       = "unicribzadmin"
$POSTGRES_PASSWORD    = "ChangeMe_Str0ng!"     # ≥ 8 chars, upper+lower+digit+symbol
$REDIS_NAME           = "unicribz-cache"       # MUST be globally unique
$STORAGE_ACCOUNT      = "unicribzstorage"      # lowercase, 3-24 chars, globally unique
$KEYVAULT_NAME        = "unicribz-kv"          # globally unique

# Show them to confirm

⚠️ Important: App Service and PostgreSQL names must be globally unique (they become *.azurewebsites.net and *.postgres.database.azure.com). If a name is taken, append a random number (e.g., unicribz-api-2026).

🗄️ Part 3: Create Azure Database for PostgreSQL
3.1 Create PostgreSQL Flexible Server
powershell
az postgres flexible-server create `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $POSTGRES_SERVER `
  --location $LOCATION `
  --admin-user $POSTGRES_ADMIN `
  --admin-password $POSTGRES_PASSWORD `
  --sku-name Standard_B1ms `
  --tier Burstable `
  --storage-size 32 `
  --version 15 `
  --public-access 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255 `
  --yes
What this does:

Standard_B1ms = 1 vCPU, 2 GB RAM — cheapest tier, ~$12/month

--public-access 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255 = allows connections from any IP. For production, restrict this to your App Service's outbound IPs later.

Creation takes 3–5 minutes. Be patient.

Expected final output:

json
{
  "fullyQualifiedDomainName": "unicribz-db.postgres.database.azure.com",
  "state": "Ready",
  "version": "15"
}
3.2 Create the Database
powershell
az postgres flexible-server db create `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --server-name $POSTGRES_SERVER `
  --database-name $DB_NAME
3.3 Allow Azure Services Through Firewall
powershell
az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule create `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $POSTGRES_SERVER `
  --rule-name AllowAzureServices `
  --start-ip-address 0.0.0.0 `
  --end-ip-address 0.0.0.0
This special rule allows any Azure service (including App Service) to connect.

3.4 Save the Connection String
powershell
$POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING = "Host=$POSTGRES_SERVER.postgres.database.azure.com;Port=5432;Database=$DB_NAME;Username=$POSTGRES_ADMIN;Password=$POSTGRES_PASSWORD;SslMode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true"

Write-Host "PostgreSQL Connection String:"
Write-Host $POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING
Copy this value somewhere safe. You'll need it in Step 7.

🔐 Part 7: Configure App Settings (Environment Variables)
App Service replaces any config in appsettings.json with environment variables. This is where your real secrets live.

7.1 Set API Environment Variables
powershell
az webapp config appsettings set `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $API_APP_NAME `
  --settings `
    "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production" `
    "ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection=$POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING" `
    "ConnectionStrings__Redis=$REDIS_CONNECTION_STRING" `
    "Jwt__Key=YourProductionJwtSecretKeyAtLeast32CharsLong!" `
    "Jwt__Issuer=UniCribz" `
    "Jwt__Audience=UniCribzClients" `
    "Jwt__ExpiryMinutes=60" `
    "App__BaseUrl=https://$API_APP_NAME.azurewebsites.net" `
    "App__WebBaseUrl=https://$WEB_APP_NAME.azurewebsites.net" `
    "App__AllowedOrigins__0=https://$WEB_APP_NAME.azurewebsites.net" `
    "Database__MigrateOnStartup=true" `
    "Database__SeedOnStartup=false" `
    "Azure__Storage__ConnectionString=$STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING" `
    "Azure__Storage__ContainerName=unicribz-files"
What these do:

Setting	Value	Purpose
ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT	Production	Loads appsettings.Production.json, enables HSTS
ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection	PostgreSQL conn string	__ = nested config in .NET
ConnectionStrings__Redis	Redis conn string	Cache
Jwt__Key	32+ char secret	Change this to your own random string!
App__AllowedOrigins__0	Web URL	CORS for frontend
Database__MigrateOnStartup	true	Runs migrations automatically on first deploy
Database__SeedOnStartup	false	Don't re-seed production
⚠️ Critical: Replace YourProductionJwtSecretKeyAtLeast32CharsLong! with a real random 32+ character secret. Generate one:

powershell
# Generate a secure JWT key
$JWT_KEY = -join ((48..57) + (65..90) + (97..122) | Get-Random -Count 48 | ForEach-Object {[char]$_})
Write-Host "Your JWT key: $JWT_KEY"
7.2 Set Web Frontend Environment Variables
powershell

  --name $WEB_APP_NAME `
  --settings `
    "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production" `

Cost Optimisation Tips
1. Stop the App Service when not in use:

powershell
az webapp stop --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $API_APP_NAME
az webapp stop --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $WEB_APP_NAME

powershell

powershell

powershell

  --start-date (Get-Date).AddDays(-30).ToString("yyyy-MM-dd") `

  --query "[?contains(instanceName, '$RESOURCE_GROUP')].{Name:instanceName, Cost:pretaxCost, Currency:currency}" `

🚨 Part 13: Troubleshooting
Symptom	Cause	Fix
503 Service Unavailable on API	App still starting or crashed	az webapp log tail --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $API_APP_NAME
/health/ready returns Unhealthy	DB or Redis unreachable	Check connection strings in app settings
Login returns 500	Migrations didn't run	Verify Database__MigrateOnStartup=true and check logs
CORS errors in browser	AllowedOrigins wrong	az webapp config appsettings list → check App__AllowedOrigins__0
Cannot connect to PostgreSQL	Firewall blocks App Service	Verify AllowAzureServices firewall rule exists
App crashes on startup	Config validation failed	Check logs — invalid JWT key or missing connection string
GitHub Actions deploy fails	Publish profile invalid	Re-download and re-add secret
Slot swap fails	Staging slot not warmed up	Wait 30s after deploy before swap (workflow already does this)
Static files 404 on Web	Static files not copied	Verify wwwroot/ is in publish output
Get detailed logs:

powershell
az webapp log tail `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $API_APP_NAME `
  --provider Application

Your cost-saving plan revolves around two key pillars: Azure for Students and Always Free services.

Create a Resource Group: Use the az group create command to create a new resource group for UniCribz. This is a logical container for all your services.

Deploy Credit-Covered Services:

Create an Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server using the Burstable, B1ms tier. This is the cheapest option and will be paid for by your $100 credit.

Create an Azure Cache for Redis using the Basic C0 tier. This will also be covered by your credit.

Use GitHub Actions (free for students) to deploy your API and Web app to the App Service Plan.

🚨 Critical: How to Guarantee You're Never Charged

NEVER Upgrade Your Subscription: Do not click "Upgrade to Pay-As-You-Go" in the Azure portal. As long as you have the "Azure for Students" offer, you are not required to have a credit card on file and Azure will not charge you. Your services will simply stop when the credit is exhausted.

Stay Within the Free Tiers: Be mindful of the limits. For example, the App Service B1 plan has a limit on CPU time and memory. If you exceed it, your app may be throttled, but you will not be charged. The biggest risk is exceeding the 5 GB Blob Storage limit; monitor your usage.

By following this plan, you can deploy and run your entire UniCribz backend on Azure for free for at least 12 months.

This guide provides a complete, step-by-step plan to deploy the UniCribz backend on Azure with zero out-of-pocket cost by leveraging the Azure for Students program and its generous free tiers.

🎓 Part 1: Activating Your Azure for Students Account
Your foundation is the Azure for Students offer, which provides a $100 credit for 12 months and does not require a credit card to sign up.

Sign Up: Go to the Azure for Students page.

Verify: Click "Activate now" and sign in with your personal Microsoft account. You will then be asked to verify your student status using your university email address.

Confirm: Once verified, your subscription is created automatically. You can view your $100 credit and free services in the Azure portal.

🏗️ Part 2: The Zero-Cost Resource Plan
This plan maps each UniCribz component to a free or credit-covered Azure service.

UniCribz Component	Recommended Azure Service	Cost Basis
UniCribz.Api (Backend)	Azure App Service (B1 Linux Plan)	Always Free
UniCribz.Web (Frontend)	Azure App Service (Shared B1 Plan)	Always Free
PostgreSQL Database	Azure Database for PostgreSQL (Burstable B1ms)	Free for 12 months

⚙️ Part 3: Step-by-Step Implementation
Step 1: Set Up Your Environment
Install the Azure CLI and sign in.

powershell
# Install Azure CLI (if not already installed)
winget install -e --id Microsoft.AzureCLI

# Sign in
az login

# Confirm you are using the student subscription
az account show
If you have multiple subscriptions, select the correct one with az account set --subscription "Azure for Students".

Step 2: Define Variables and Create a Resource Group
Set your unique names. App Service and PostgreSQL names must be globally unique.

powershell
$RESOURCE_GROUP = "unicribz-rg"
$LOCATION = "southafricanorth"
$APP_SERVICE_PLAN = "unicribz-plan"
$API_APP_NAME = "unicribz-api-2026"   # CHANGE to a unique name
$WEB_APP_NAME = "unicribz-web-2026"   # CHANGE to a unique name
$POSTGRES_SERVER = "unicribz-db-2026" # CHANGE to a unique name
$POSTGRES_ADMIN = "unicribzadmin"
$POSTGRES_PASSWORD = "YourStr0ng!Pass" # CHANGE to a strong password
$DB_NAME = "unicribz_prod"

az group create --name $RESOURCE_GROUP --location $LOCATION
Step 3: Provision Free-Tier Services
1. Create a single Free App Service Plan (Linux, B1)
This plan will host both your API and Web app at no cost.

powershell
az appservice plan create `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $APP_SERVICE_PLAN `
  --location $LOCATION `
  --sku B1 `
  --is-linux
2. Create Blob Storage (Always Free)
The first 5 GB are free.

powershell
$STORAGE_ACCOUNT = "unicribzstorage2026" # CHANGE to a unique name

az storage account create `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $STORAGE_ACCOUNT `
  --location $LOCATION `
  --sku Standard_LRS

az storage container create `
  --account-name $STORAGE_ACCOUNT `
  --name unicribz-files `
  --auth-mode login
Step 4: Provision Credit-Covered Services
1. Create PostgreSQL (Free for 12 months)
This uses the free Burstable B1ms tier, perfect for development and testing.

powershell
az postgres flexible-server create `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $POSTGRES_SERVER `
  --location $LOCATION `
  --admin-user $POSTGRES_ADMIN `
  --admin-password $POSTGRES_PASSWORD `
  --sku-name Standard_B1ms `
  --tier Burstable `
  --storage-size 32 `
  --public-access 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255 `
  --yes

az postgres flexible-server db create `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --server-name $POSTGRES_SERVER `
  --database-name $DB_NAME
2. Create Redis Cache (Free for 12 months)
This uses the free Basic C0 tier.

powershell
$REDIS_NAME = "unicribz-cache-2026" # CHANGE to a unique name

az redis create `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $REDIS_NAME `
  --location $LOCATION `
  --sku Basic `
  --vm-size c0 `
  --enable-non-ssl-port false
Step 5: Create App Services for API and Web
powershell
az webapp create --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --plan $APP_SERVICE_PLAN --name $API_APP_NAME --runtime "DOTNETCORE:8.0"
az webapp create --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --plan $APP_SERVICE_PLAN --name $WEB_APP_NAME --runtime "DOTNETCORE:8.0"
Step 6: Configure Environment Variables (Secrets)
Retrieve the connection strings and inject them into the App Service settings.

powershell
# --- Get Secrets ---
$POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING = "Host=$POSTGRES_SERVER.postgres.database.azure.com;Port=5432;Database=$DB_NAME;Username=$POSTGRES_ADMIN;Password=$POSTGRES_PASSWORD;SslMode=Require"
$REDIS_HOST = "$REDIS_NAME.redis.cache.windows.net"
$REDIS_KEY = az redis list-keys --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $REDIS_NAME --query primaryKey --output tsv
$REDIS_CONNECTION_STRING = "$REDIS_HOST`:6380,password=$REDIS_KEY,ssl=True,abortConnect=False"
$STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING = az storage account show-connection-string --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $STORAGE_ACCOUNT --query connectionString --output tsv
$JWT_KEY = -join ((48..57) + (65..90) + (97..122) | Get-Random -Count 48 | ForEach-Object {[char]$_}) # Generates a secure key

# --- Apply to API App Service ---
az webapp config appsettings set `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $API_APP_NAME `
  --settings `
    "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production" `
    "ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection=$POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING" `
    "ConnectionStrings__Redis=$REDIS_CONNECTION_STRING" `
    "Jwt__Key=$JWT_KEY" `
    "App__BaseUrl=https://$API_APP_NAME.azurewebsites.net" `
    "App__WebBaseUrl=https://$WEB_APP_NAME.azurewebsites.net" `
    "App__AllowedOrigins__0=https://$WEB_APP_NAME.azurewebsites.net" `
    "Database__MigrateOnStartup=true" `
    "Database__SeedOnStartup=false" `
    "Azure__Storage__ConnectionString=$STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING"

# --- Apply to Web App Service ---
az webapp config appsettings set `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $WEB_APP_NAME `
  --settings `
    "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production" `
    "Api__BaseUrl=https://$API_APP_NAME.azurewebsites.net"
Note: Database__SeedOnStartup=true is used only for the first deployment. You will disable it immediately afterward.

Step 7: Deploy Your Code and Seed the Database
Deploy API: In Visual Studio, right-click UniCribz.Api → Publish → Azure → Azure App Service (Linux) → select your $API_APP_NAME.

Deploy Web: Repeat the process for UniCribz.Web, selecting $WEB_APP_NAME.

Seed Database: The API will start and run migrations. Since SeedOnStartup is true, it will also insert the default users.

powershell
# Trigger a restart to ensure seeding runs
az webapp restart --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $API_APP_NAME
Disable Seeding (CRITICAL): Once you have verified the login works, turn off the seeder.

powershell
az webapp config appsettings set `
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP `
  --name $API_APP_NAME `
  --settings "Database__SeedOnStartup=false"
Step 8: Verify Deployment
powershell
# Check API health (Readiness)
Invoke-RestMethod "https://$API_APP_NAME.azurewebsites.net/health/ready"
# Expected: {"status":"Healthy","checks":{"postgresql":"Healthy","redis":"Healthy"}}

# Test login (once seeded)
$body = @{ email = "admin@unicribz.co.za"; password = "Admin@123" } | ConvertTo-Json
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://$API_APP_NAME.azurewebsites.net/api/auth/login" -Method POST -Body $body -ContentType "application/json"
# Expected: A JSON object containing a "token".

Set Budget Alerts: In the Azure Portal, go to Cost Management + Billing → Budgets. Create a budget for your resource group with alerts at $10, $50, and $90. You will be notified long before the credit is used up.

Stop Services When Not in Use: If you are not actively developing or demonstrating, stop the expensive services.

powershell
# Stop App Service

az postgres flexible-server stop --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $POSTGRES_SERVER

# Stop Redis (pauses billing)
az redis update --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $REDIS_NAME --set "properties.publicNetworkAccess=Disabled" # Basic C0 has no stop, this effectively disables it
To resume:

powershell
az webapp start --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $API_APP_NAME
az webapp start --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $WEB_APP_NAME
az postgres flexible-server start --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $POSTGRES_SERVER
az redis update --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $REDIS_NAME --set "properties.publicNetworkAccess=Enabled"
🗑️ Part 5: Final Cleanup
When the project is completely finished, delete the entire resource group to stop all charges permanently.

powershell
az group delete --name $RESOURCE_GROUP --yes --no-wait
🚨 Important Notes & Limitations
App Service Free Tier Limits: The B1 plan gives you 60 minutes of CPU time per day and 1 GB of memory. This is fine for development and demos but will throttle if you have sustained high traffic.

Swagger in Production: For security, Swagger is disabled in the Production environment. To test endpoints in the cloud, you can temporarily set ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Staging in your App Service settings, restart the app, and then set it back to Production.

Scaling: If you need more performance, you can scale up the App Service Plan to a higher tier, but this will begin to consume your $100 credit.

This zero-cost architecture provides a complete, production-ready environment for the UniCribz project. Follow the steps, keep an eye on your budget alerts, and you can run your entire application on Azure for free.

If you run into any issues during setup, let me know and we can troubleshoot them together.
